land.text: Tlemcen: 'In 1066, the Almoravids under Ibn Tashfin captured Tlemcen'

successors.note: The page also says the Banu Ifran were 'defeated by the Almoravids and the invading Banu Hilal and Banu Sulaym at the end of the 11th century'. The Barghawata dossier has the Almoravids take Tamesna by 1060.

capitals.name: Tlemcen
capitals.note: The page says Abu Qurra 'founded the city of Tlemcen in this region in 765' and names no capital for the Ifranids before Salé; it also names Ifgan as a new capital after Ya'la ibn Mohammed took Oran (no year, Ifgan not placed here). Tlemcen is the researcher's choice.

capitals.name: Salé
capitals.note: Temim 'built the city in 1030' and died in Salé (Chellah) in 1054-55; the Banu Ifran page says Abu al-Kamal 'established a new capital at Salé' with no year. The Tlemcen emirate went on to 1058 or 1066 on the page (Abu Soda killed in 1058).

correction.text: Tlemcen and Oran, the Ifranid country of the west Maghreb in the page's 950-1066 span

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page has no infobox and no frontier; the navbox gives 'Ifrinid Dynasty 950-1066'. Tlemcen (founded by Abu Qurra in 765) and Oran (taken by Ya'la ibn Mohammed, no year) are the only places the page ties to the dynasty before 993; the circles are mine.

correction.text: Tlemcen, Oran and Fez, which Yaddu ibn Ya'la 'took by surprise in January 993' and held 'for some months'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, one year. Ziri recaptured Fez in 993 (Ziri ibn Atiyya page), so the Fez circle belongs to 993 alone.

correction.text: Tlemcen and Oran again; the page names no gain or loss between 993 and 1029

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Bridging: the page is silent on these 35 years.

correction.text: Tlemcen, Oran and Tamesna, which Temim 'conquered... from the Barghawata' in 1029 (Salé built 1030)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1029, Temim expedited to Tamesna' and expelled half the population; the Tamesna shape is the Barghawata Conference row of 1015 as the sibling dossier draws it. That dossier has the Almoravids conquer the Barghawata 'by 1060', so the two dossiers overlap on Tamesna.

correction.text: Tlemcen, Oran, Tamesna and Fez, which Temim seized from the Maghrawa leader Hammama in May-June 1033

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The killings took place in the month of Jumaada al-Akhir 424 AH (May-June 1033 AD)'; the Maghrawa recapture of Fez is dated 1037-1038 here, 1039 on the Temim page and 1038-1040 on the Banu Ifran page, so 1038 is the last year of the Fez circle.

correction.text: Tlemcen, Oran and the Salé-Chellah country, where Temim took refuge after losing Fez; control 'as far as Tadla' (no year)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Temim died in 1054-55 in Salé, specifically in Chellah, which he had conquered after fleeing from Hammama in 1038-39.' The page says the Ifrenid emirate fell in 1058 after the Hilalian invasion and gives 1066 for the Almoravid capture of Tlemcen; the Tamesna circle is dropped from 1039 because the page does not say what became of it.

ledger.note: 950 (page silent on land): the navbox gives 'Ifrinid Dynasty 950-1066'. The page does not say where the dynasty ruled in 950; Tlemcen (founded 765 by Abu Qurra) and Oran (captured by Ya'la ibn Mohammed, undated) are the places it ties to the Ifranids. The page dates the 'dynasty' to 'the 10th century' in its text and has an 'emirate' at Tlemcen from 765; the two are not reconciled.

January 993: Yaddu ibn Ya'la takes Fez. 'Yaddu ibn Ya'la took Fes by surprise in January 993' and held it 'for some months' until the Maghrawa ruler Ziri ibn Atiyya reconquered the region (Maghrawa dossier: Ziri 'recaptured Fes in 993 and displayed Yaddu's severed head on its walls'). [Reviewer af-02-x: month dropped so the January gain can precede the undated loss of later in 993; the ledger had the loss first.]
993: Ziri ibn Atiyya recaptures Fez. 'Ziri... recaptured Fes in 993 and displayed Yaddu's severed head on its walls'; the Banu Ifran page says only that the town was held 'for some months'.

region.text: Tamesna, the Barghawata country on the Atlantic coast

ledger.note: 1029: Temim conquers Tamesna from the Barghawata. 'In 1029, Temim expedited to Tamesna' and 'eradicated false Barghawata doctrines, expelled half of the population'; the Banu Ifran page: 'conquered Tamesna from the Barghawata' in 1029.

1030 (bridge): Salé becomes the Ifranid capital. The Temim page says he 'built the city in 1030' and the Banu Ifran page that Abu al-Kamal (Temim) 'established a new capital at Salé' with no year, so 1030 is the year of the building, not of a dated capital move.

May-June 1033: Temim seizes Fez from the Maghrawa. 'In 1033, Temim, leading troops of the Banu Ifran, seized Fez, Morocco from under Maghrawa leader Hammama'; the killings 'took place in the month of Jumaada al-Akhir 424 AH (May-June 1033 AD)'.

1038: Hammama retakes Fez. The 1033 Fez massacre page: Hammama 'recaptured Fez in 1037-1038, forcing Tamim to flee to Salé'; the Temim page has 'reconquered Fez in 1039' and the Banu Ifran page 1038-1040. 1038 is the middle reading.

region.text: Salé and Chellah on the Bou Regreg

ledger.note: 1038-39: Temim takes Chellah after fleeing Fez. 'Temim died in 1054-55 in Salé, specifically in Chellah, which he had conquered after fleeing from Hammama in 1038-39'; his control reached 'as far as Tadla' (no year). The page does not say who held Chellah.

region.text: Tlemcen, Oran and the Salé country

ledger.note: 1066: the Almoravids take Tlemcen. 'In 1066, the Almoravids under Ibn Tashfin captured Tlemcen' and 'finished off the tribes'; the navbox ends the dynasty in 1066. The page also says the Ifrenid emirate 'fell' in 1058 after the Hilalian invasion, with the Hammadid Buluggin ibn Muhammad sacking Tlemcen the same year, and that the Banu Ifran were defeated 'at the end of the 11th century'.

wars.name: Buluggin ibn Ziri's western expedition

zones.text: Fez, Sijilmasa and the Barghawata country

wars.outcome: Buluggin 'left Ifriqiya on 27 March 979... and marched on Fez, which he captured with relative ease', then campaigned to Sijilmasa and against the Barghawata; the Ifranid governors retreated towards Ceuta; he died on 25 May 984 between Sijilmasa and Tlemcen; afterwards 'the Maghrawa and the Banu Ifran began to reclaim the towns and territories which he had just conquered'.
wars.note: The page does not say that the Banu Ifran themselves held Fez in 979.

wars.name: Yaddu's seizure of Fez
wars.outcome: Yaddu ibn Ya'la took Fez by surprise in January 993; Ziri ibn Atiyya recaptured it the same year and displayed Yaddu's head on the walls.

wars.name: Ifranid-Maghrawa struggle for Fez
wars.outcome: Temim seized Fez in May-June 1033 and massacred some 6,000 Jews; Hammama retook it in 1037-1039 and Temim withdrew to Salé and Chellah.

wars.name: Hilalian and Almoravid end of the Ifranid emirate
wars.outcome: The emirate fell in 1058 after the Hilalian invasion; the Hammadid Buluggin ibn Muhammad sacked Tlemcen that year; the Almoravids under Ibn Tashfin took Tlemcen in 1066.
wars.note: The page's own dates for the fall (1058, 1066) are not reconciled.

certainty.note: A tribal dynasty on thin pages: the circles around Tlemcen, Oran, Fez and Salé are the researcher's; only the years of the Fez and Tamesna moves are the pages'.

notes: Cliopatria has no Banu Ifran row. The Banu Ifran page has no infobox; the navbox gives 950-1066 and the text an Abu Qurra emirate at Tlemcen from 765 (the sibling Idrisid report names Abu Qurra's Tlemcen in 789), with the 8th-century revolt against the Umayyads and Abbasids and the c.547-550 clash with John Troglita as undated background; the dossier starts in 950 because nothing connects the 765 emirate to the 10th-century dynasty on the pages opened. The page says Ya'la ibn Mohammed was killed by Jawhar 'in battle in 954' (a footnote cites Ibn Khaldun for 958) and that the Fatimids destroyed Ifgan; none is placed or dated closely enough for a ledger event. Pages disagree on the Maghrawa recapture of Fez (1037-1038, 1039, 1038-1040). The Ifranid founding of the Taifa of Ronda (1039; Abu Nur lord of Ronda and Seville 1023-1039 per the page) is al-Andalus and is left to the Iberia group. The Barghawata dossier has no 1029 loss; its Tamesna loss is to the Almoravids by 1060, so the two dossiers conflict on who held Tamesna after 1029. The Maghrawa dossier has the matching 993 and 1033/1038 Fez events; the Idrisid dossier's Tlemcen events from 789 are not matched here.
